2607.17673.title: Beyond Objective Expressivity: Geometry Preservation in Multimodal Contrastive Learning
2607.17673.paper_summary: Contrastive learning is increasingly moving toward settings with three or more modalities instead of image-text pairs. Yet, extending models from pairwise to higher-order multimodal alignment can introduce optimization and representation challenges. We identify encoder Jacobian conditioning as a key factor in trimodal contrastive learning: poorly conditioned encoders exhibit collapsing or amplified singular-value spectra, leading to exploding Jacobian condition numbers and degraded multimodal alignment. We introduce geometry-preserving encoders (GPEs) by directly conditioning the Jacobian through regularization and demonstrating that simple modifications like LeakyReLU activations and residual paths recover these geometric benefits. Across a synthetic benchmark and four real-world datasets including missing modalities, improving Jacobian conditioning boosts retrieval and linear probe performance across multiple contrastive objectives, whereas expressive objectives yield little benefit in linear probes. More broadly, our results show that multimodal contrastive learning depends not only on objective expressivity, but also on the geometric and optimization properties of the underlying encoders.
2607.17673.paper_summary_zh: 對比學習越來越多地朝著三種或更多模態的設置發展，而不是僅僅是圖像-文本對。然而，將模型從成對擴展到更高階的多模態對齊可能會引入優化和表示的挑戰。我們確定編碼器雅可比條件作為三模對比學習中的一個關鍵因素：條件不良的編碼器會顯示出崩潰或放大的奇異值光譜，導致雅可比條件數爆炸和多模態對齊的退化。我們通過正則化直接調整雅可比，介紹了幾何保持編碼器（GPEs），並展示了像LeakyReLU激活和殘差路徑這樣的簡單修改如何恢復這些幾何優勢。在一個合成基準和四個包括缺失模態的真實世界數據集中，改善雅可比條件提升了多個對比目標下的檢索和線性探測性能，而表達性目標在線性探測中幾乎沒有好處。更廣泛地說，我們的結果顯示，多模態對比學習不僅依賴於目標的表達性，還依賴於基礎編碼器的幾何和優化特性。
